title: Elementwise passes with runtime extents through our emitter
description: The DSL's product/copy_from plan their loops from static box extents and panic on a runtime axis. With runtime extents, the per-element pass (and a recipe's output copy) is our emitter's code inside the tile kernel, as sk8's dynamic mode does by hand.

title: Launcher: take CubeCL kernels' grid-constant info struct and dynamic metadata
description: Tile kernels take __grid_constant__ info_st by value plus a dynamic_meta pointer; our launcher and build.py accept only the pointer ABI (grid_constants refused). Definitions can be built without launching (#[cube(launch, create_dummy_kernel)], placeholder Handle::new) in the compiler process.

Our route uses CompilationOptions::default(), where the cubecl-cpp metadata pass emits one info pointer, our ABI. Design decision 2 builds tile kernels with our KernelBuilder, no Launcher/TileArg, so launcher and metadata stay unchanged. title: Non-sum combine across planes (max/min/prod slot read)

title: Vector-valued recipes
description: Procedural reads are scalar by an explicit assert. Add a vector evaluate (default: one lane at a time) and have our recipe emit vector loads through our emitter. Note: a 4-wide line cannot be masked, so vector loads apply to rows of whole steps (sk8).

title: Bounds-safe recipes: test bounds before evaluating
description: ProceduralExpand read_checked/read_masked evaluate the recipe, then select; with a memory-reading recipe a partial tile reads past the tensor (sk8: up to 28 floats past x at 4099). Memory tiles redirect out-of-range indices first. In our copy: evaluate at a redirected coordinate or pass the in-bounds predicate so our emitter's guarded loads apply. Memcheck cannot see it under CubeCL's pools; test under PyTorch allocations. Must land before anything ships.
notes: Run-time proof (2026-10-30, fused_probe ... validate): CubeCL's validate_index in the summing recipe reports 29 OOB indices into x at 2048x4099 (8394752..8394780 = row 2047, cols 4099..4127); none at 2048x8192; output still correct (masked after the load). Memcheck cannot see it under CubeCL's pools. A regression test for this bead can use the same validate hook.

title: Load cache hints in the tile memory loads (retained / streaming)
description: The DSL has no hint syntax; sk8 set the CubeCL patch's LoadOp flags by walking the expanded IR. Without them the second pass re-reads the row from DRAM (286 vs 204 us). Add a hint to tile reads in our copy and set it from the plan (first pass retained, last streaming), as our emitter and Triton do.
notes: Settled for stage 1 by design decision 3 of cubecl-tile-stage-1: all row reads go through recipes calling our emitter, which sets hints through descriptor op flags; no DSL hint syntax needed unless a memory tile is read.

title: Summation order in our copy: tree plane combine, lane tree, xor 16->1
description: The DSL fixes the order in its lowering: units xor 1..16 (space/share.rs), planes in sequence (slot read sums in writer order), lanes in sequence. Triton: pairwise tree in-thread, lanes xor 16..1, warps as a tree. docs/research/sk8/order_model.py models both bit for bit; with all three changes rows closer/farther than Triton 793/811 (normal) and 314/353 (offset). Verify on GPU and through welford_band; bit-identical results would also need Triton's thread ownership.

title: Assess cubecl-tile (CubeCL's tile DSL) as the kernel-to-thread mapping for cubecl_torch
description: CubeCL's tile DSL (crates/cubecl-tile, ~43k lines; cubek-tile in CubeK since 2026-05-29, reductions since 2026-08-17, moved into CubeCL 2026-10-22, present at our pin 907676dc) maps tiles to cubes/planes/units and provides matmul, product, monoid reduce and online softmax. CubeK matmul/attention/microkernels build on it. cubecl_torch hand-builds that mapping per plan from raw IR, and the Triton gaps (4z8.37/39/40, 6cl, 9hg, 4z8.34, 4x9.16/17) are that mapping arriving piece by piece. Questions: (1) do its reduce/softmax cover Inductor's kernels (fused loop bodies, multi-pass rows, Welford, multi-output, split/cooperative finals); (2) how it picks the split across levels vs Triton's rules (num_warps, XBLOCK, blocked layouts); (3) control of accumulation order for Triton's accuracy band; (4) fit with descriptor-driven building and our launcher (does it need a CubeCL Client?); (5) what of reduction/emit.rs, plan.rs and legality would go. Outcome: a recommendation (adopt / adopt for part / not) with evidence, before transcendentals (4x9.3). Per rule reuse-the-mechanism (user 2026-10-30).
notes:
First pass 2026-10-30 (source reading, no GPU runs). History: cubek-tile since 2026-05-29, tile reductions since 2026-08-17 (#489); moved into CubeCL 2026-10-22; at our pin. Fast-moving: 187 cubek-tile commits since 2026-09-01, 16 in cubecl-tile since the move. Never assessed by cubecl_torch; Stage 5 only compiled it as a dependency.
MECHANISM PRESENT: a Partitioning = Space cut into Levels, each level distributing axes over cube/plane/unit (power-of-two counts) or walking them. Reductions follow from the partitioning: space/share.rs UnitShare derives which unit-index bits hold partials of one cell and emits plane_sum or plane_shuffle_xor over exactly those bits (Triton-style layout-derived reduction). Across planes: shared-memory accumulators (atomic smem_accumulation, cyclic rounds smem_cyclic, smem_slots = fixed writer order, bit-reproducible). Across cubes: split as an axis (two passes), relay, last_arrival, Levels::shared_by. Also OnlineSoftmax, staging pipelines (Stages), vectorization requirements, procedural tiles, Launcher reading the grid off the levels.
POLICY ABSENT: the caller states the levels; cubecl-tile does not choose them (CubeK routines/microkernels do, for matmul/attention). Inductor's Triton config (XBLOCK, R0_BLOCK, num_warps) could be translated into Levels.
GAPS: Monoid is a closed enum Sum/Prod/Max/Min (no Welford, argmax, compensated sum, xor_sum) - upstream extension needed; no arbitrary elementwise tile op (only product/cast/scale/procedural), so Inductor's fused loop body would run per element at the leaves; Launcher and TileArg go through a CubeCL Client/TensorArg (same foreign-memory constraint) - unknown whether a tile kernel can be expanded through KernelBuilder and launched by our launcher; accumulation order vs Triton and speed unmeasured. cubek-reduce does not use cubecl-tile.
NEXT: one prototype - f32 sum consumer or softmax at 2048x8192 with Levels matching Triton's config (R0_BLOCK 2048, 16 warps), built without a Client if possible and launched by our launcher; compare bits and ncu time against Triton and our plane_shared plan. Answers launch fit, order and speed together.
PROTOTYPE 2026-10-30 (3080, ncu base clocks, f32 sum consumer x*x.sum(-1,keepdim) at 2048x8192; scratch crate tile_proto against pinned CubeCL, CubeCL CUDA runtime with cuda-cpp so the C++ backend + NVRTC 13.0 from the venv wheels, as production). Triton (re-measured): autotune picks R0_BLOCK 8192, 16 warps: 203.9 us, 67 MB DRAM read, 34 regs. Its tl.sum is a full pairwise tree (in-thread treeReduce over 16 registers, lanes xor 16..1, then warps) - likely why our sequential-accumulating plans fall outside its band.
Tile kernels (both correct): (A) Triton-shaped, one row per cube, 16 planes x 32 units x vec4 split K, walk 4, planes meet via smem_cyclic_accumulation, product pass at cube level: 287.0 us, 129 MB read, 34 regs, 83% occupancy; accuracy: normal data mean sum error 8.4e-6 vs Triton 7.2e-6 (rows closer/farther 721/919), offset 0.37 vs 0.22 (274/887), ~19-42% rows bitwise = Triton. (B) one row per plane, 16 rows/cube: 295 us, 134 MB.
Gap to Triton is DRAM re-read in the second pass (no L1 reuse); the DSL exposes no load cache hints (Triton evict_last; our patched set_retained). Lowering notes: pass 1 adds each float4 into one scalar per unit per step (not per-lane accumulators + tree); the cyclic plane combine repeats the plane shuffle and a barrier in each of 16 rounds.
API lessons: a level only distributes work when iterated (for unit in &step); without it every unit computed the whole row and the sum came out 32x (my misuse, not a defect). smem_slots drain takes no region (failed at plane level); cyclic drain_at works. The cyclic accumulator needs 2-D boxes (sums as [M,N] with N=1). CubeCL's CUDA runtime defaults to LLVM NVPTX at this pin; cuda-cpp gave identical bits.
LAUNCH FIT: #[cube(launch, create_dummy_kernel)] builds the kernel struct and define() -> KernelDefinition from device/target properties and launch args without launching; Handle::new is public (placeholder handles). The tile Launcher needs a Client (fine in our separate compiler process). ABI differs: tile kernels take __grid_constant__ info_st by value + dynamic_meta pointer; our launcher accepts only the pointer ABI (build.py refuses grid_constants) -> launcher extension needed. Not implemented.
Prototype sources were in the session scratchpad only (tile_proto/src/main.rs, triton_ref.py, compare.py, triton_time.py).
Prototype sources saved to docs/research/sk8 (README has results and run commands).
EXPERIMENTS 2026-10-30 (docs/research/sk8 README has tables). (1) Load hints set during expansion (helper walks the IR, sets the CubeCL patch's LoadOp retained/streaming flags on 16-byte global loads): tile kernel 204.0 us / 70 MB vs Triton 203.9 / 67 on the 3080; 169.5 / 71 vs 167.0 / 67 on the 3090. Without hints 286 / 129. So speed parity needs only load hints the DSL lacks. (2) Order: order_model.py reproduces Triton's GPU output and the tile kernels' bit for bit. Per-lane accumulators (lanes mode, also at Triton speed: 204.7 us / 67 MB) help offset data (0.37 -> 0.26 mean sum error; Triton 0.187) but not normal (8.25e-6; Triton 6.96e-6). Modelled fixes: planes combined as a tree is the biggest gain (normal 7.09e-6, offset 0.221); plus lanes as a tree and units xor 16->1: 7.04e-6 / 0.191, closer/farther vs Triton 793/811 and 314/353 (likely passes the sign-test half of the band; not run through welford_band). Bitwise Triton would also need its ownership (repeats 2048 apart). The DSL fixes the order in its lowering (units xor 1..16, planes sequential via cyclic rounds, lanes sequential): reaching Triton's accuracy needs DSL changes (a tree plane combine; a choice of xor direction; a tree lane combine) or our own lowering of those steps. Pitfall: two bindings of one buffer make the second const __restrict__ (non-coherent loads) and it cannot see in-kernel writes.
CHECKS 2026-10-30 (docs/research/sk8 README, fused_probe/). (1) Fused loop bodies: Inductor's RMSNorm-with-weight semantic.json (x^2 before the sum; /N, +eps, rsqrt, *x, *w after) runs inside tile loops through two hand-written recipes that call our semantic::emit unchanged (ir.rs/semantic.rs compiled in via #[path]). Correct (max rel err 2.6e-7 vs f64). 3080 ncu: tile 229.8-231.3 us / 85.6-86.7 MB, Triton 228.6-231.0 / 85, ours today (shared_tree_compensated 512) ~223 / 85.7. Limits: recipe values are scalar (no vector loads; no cost here, memory-bound); procedural copy needs a scalar destination; recipes are documented memory-free (overhang/staging untested); the row sum must come back through a writable second binding (a read-only one is const __restrict__ non-coherent); only plain ops + one sum tried. (2) Compile time per kernel: tile ~67 ms (expand 7.6 incl emit 0.1, C++ 30, NVRTC 29 on 1188 lines) vs ours ~32 ms (compiler process 10-12, NVRTC 20 on 363 lines). Note: adding the probe inside native/ behind an off-by-default feature changed the default binary digest (Cargo crate hash) -> would invalidate all artifact keys; the probe is a separate crate instead.
PRE-ADOPTION CHECKS 2026-10-30 (README 'Checks before adoption'). Runtime extents: correct on 13 shapes incl. 4099, 65539, 7x2049; one kernel per alignment class (4-wide only for rows of whole 128-wide steps: a vector line cannot be masked; scalar unmasked; scalar masked); no cost (204.3 us at 8192 = fixed-size; 101.2 vs Triton 101.6 at 2048x4099). The DSL's elementwise ops (product, copy_from) need static box extents, so with runtime extents the elementwise pass is plain cube code (our emitter's job anyway). Partial tiles with recipes: correct, but recipes are evaluated before the bounds test (read_checked evaluates then selects) -> up to 28 floats read past the tensor at 4099; memory tiles redirect indices first. Fix in our copy. Combines: cross-plane/cross-cube destinations only add (max/min/prod refused); accumulator cells are one number, so Welford/argmax need a multi-value cell (real extension). Vector recipes: scalar by explicit assert; local change. Layout: planes_across + slots (CubeK InSlots) gives 308-line kernels, ~31 ms compile (= ours) and RMSNorm 216.8 us / 78.8 MB vs Triton 228.6-231.0 and ours ~223; the earlier 67 ms came from the cyclic combine's 16 unrolled rounds. Compute Sanitizer is not installed on the Linux side.
Compute Sanitizer (system install, 2026.3) runs under WSL; memcheck on the 4099 fused probe, with and without --padding 4096: 0 errors, because CubeCL pools tensors in larger blocks so the 28-float overrun stays inside owned memory. The recipe OOB evidence stays the generated code (load before select).
close_reason: Assessment complete (docs/research/sk8): adopt cubecl-tile in stages, taking the code into our tree; stage 1 is epic f05 (row-sum reductions), Welford/argmax deferred to 8im.

title: Signed int32/int64 add/sub/mul/neg overflow is C++ UB that NVRTC exploits
description: Found 2026-10-26 while planning integer abs (4x9.2 group 3). semantic.rs emits signed add/sub/mul as CubeCL IAddOp/ISubOp/IMulOp and neg as SNegOp, printed as C++ signed int/long long arithmetic; signed overflow is undefined, and NVRTC folds compares on it. Probe (int64 storage, cast to int32/int64 in-kernel, 3080): (x+1)>x is True at INT_MAX for int32 and int64, (x-1)<x True at INT_MIN, (-x)<0 for int64 INT_MIN wrong; eager and Inductor+Triton both wrap (all 8 cases OK under Triton). Violates integer-arithmetic 'Wrapping integer arithmetic' (its tests store results; no compare consumes an overflowed value). int8/int16 are safe (C++ promotes to int). Fix: compute signed add/sub/mul/neg in the unsigned type of the same width (ReinterpretCastOp to u32/u64, wrapping op, reinterpret back), which is free on the GPU; add the probe's compare cases to test_integer_arithmetic.py. Integer abs (4x9.2) needs the same helper.
notes: Fixed: semantic.rs wrapping()/wrapping_type() run signed add/sub/mul/neg and left shift in the unsigned type of the same width (every signed width). Manifest: 4 cases (embedding_backward 257x7, training 5x9; negative-index normalization idx + size) changed IR/CUDA only, PTX identical. Signed left shift was UB too but neither CubeCL nor Triton miscompiled it in probes; routed anyway. Left as is: INT_MIN / -1 and INT_MIN % -1 (UB in eager's own CUDA source too; runtime divisors cannot be folded).
close_reason: Closed

title: First-use tuning aborts compilation when a reassociated float sum differs from the baseline by more than 2e-5 (kohaku rms_norm backward)
description: Found by the integer-value-arithmetic census rerun (2026-10-25, scoreboard/results/int-inventory): kohaku_moss_ops now fails at its first region (rms_norm, admitted since int32 index_expr values compile). Its backward reduction sum_j w_j*x_ij (8612 rows x 3072, bf16 x, fp32 w, fp32 accumulation) has rows that cancel to ~0.06 from terms of size ~1. tuning.compare checks every candidate against the baseline with rtol=atol=2e-5 (schema 3) and raises, which aborts the compile. Measured against the fp64 sum: baseline max error 2.43e-5, candidates 2.16e-5 (plane_shared 256 v2) to 4.21e-5 (independent_planes); all far below the fp32 summation bound n*eps*sum|terms|; failing: shared_tree 64, plane_shared 64, plane_shared 128 v4, independent_planes 32x4/32x8. So this is reassociation, not codegen. Decide the policy: a tolerance scaled to the reduction's magnitude (e.g. relative to max|expected| or to sum|terms| when available), and/or exclude a mismatching candidate (keep the baseline, record the reason) instead of aborting. Reproduce: rms_norm from KohakuMossTrainer EAGER table with build_kohaku_moss_ops inputs, forward+backward under cubecl.
notes: Agreed design (2026-10-25): (1) a candidate failing its runtime comparison is excluded, never aborts the compile: keep the baseline and the other candidates, and record the exclusion first-class in selection.json (correctness false, excluded 'runtime_corruption_guard', max_abs_difference, guard). (2) Ordinary float-sum candidates are checked by a scale-aware runtime corruption guard (~2e-5 x max(1, max|baseline|) for float32) instead of elementwise rtol/atol. It separates observed reassociation (~4e-5 here) from gross codegen failures (a dropped/doubled term, ~1); it is NOT a bound on summation error (an all-cancelling output keeps max|baseline| near 0), and numerical admissibility stays a separate, offline policy. Non-reduction comparisons, bit-exact max/min/Welford-count checks and the Welford and qualified-plan guards stay unchanged. (3) The test suite keeps mismatches loud: strict mode (exclusion raises) in tests, so the corpus has zero unexpected exclusions.
close_reason: Fixed in 73beb0e2: scale-aware corruption guard for float sums, exclusion instead of abort (recorded in selection.json), strict mode in tests and the corpus runner. kohaku census completes (cubecl 2, rejected 9).

title: Prove index divisors/moduli positive under dynamic shapes (GroupNorm channels per group)
description: cubecl_torch/compiler/indexing.py encode() requires sympy .is_positive for ModularIndexing moduli and FloorDiv/Mod divisors. Under dynamic=True GroupNorm's index uses s_C//32 (channels per group), which sympy cannot prove positive, so dynamic GroupNorm is rejected before fusion: 'index modulus must be provably positive: ModularIndexing(p1*(((s53**2*((s27//32)) + 4)//5)) + p2, 1, s53**2*((s27//32)))' (found by welford-reductions band run 2026-10-24, group_norm-*-1x320x64x64-dynamic). sd-scripts compiles with dynamic=True, so SDXL GroupNorm regions likely hit this after Welford lands. Options: prove positivity from the shape env's value ranges / install a guard (V.graph.sizevars) when the expression is positive for all valid inputs (C >= groups), or a runtime launch check of derived divisors. Related: 4z8.18 (Max() in symbolic layouts).
acceptance_criteria: Dynamic GroupNorm (dynamic=True, 1x320x64x64 and SDXL shapes) compiles through CubeCL and matches eager; no unsound positivity assumption (guard or runtime check covers C < groups).

title: Multi-output reduction kernels: mean, rstd and normalized output in one kernel
description: The fusion rule 'one disjoint external output required' (inductor/reduction_checks.py, semantic_checks.py) and descriptor5's outputs==1 plan checks make every external output its own kernel. Norm kernels write 2-3 outputs (Triton probes 2026-10-23: GroupNorm split first stage mean/m2/weight, second stage mean/rstd; LayerNorm 4096x1280 mean/rstd/normalized output; small GroupNorm persistent mean/rstd/output), so with OpenSpec welford-reductions each output recomputes the Welford reduction in its own kernel: correct, but up to 3x Triton's work. Lift the single-output rule for reduction kernels (several stores of reduced values and reduction-scope outputs per kernel) and check the Triton performance floor for norms here (reduction-kernels spec: Welford floor deferred to this bead). Welford single-kernel timings from welford-reductions 5.1 are recorded on this bead.
acceptance_criteria: GroupNorm/LayerNorm/var_mean forward compile with Triton's kernel count and outputs per kernel; Triton performance floor met or short-kernel exceptions recorded; manifest unchanged for existing single-output kernels.
notes:
2026-10-24 Welford timing (welford-reductions 5, RTX 3080, cubecl_torch/testing/results/welford-timing.json): CubeCL/Triton device us per call: var_mean f32 37x129 3.8/1.6, f32 300x4096 12.0/9.7, bf16 300x4096 9.1/5.2, f32 8x300000 61/20; LayerNorm bf16 4096x1280 76/41, f32 129/66; GroupNorm 1x320x64x64 f32 47/27, bf16 30/12. Most of the gap is one kernel per output (2-5 kernels each repeating the reduction vs Triton's one). The Welford plan rule (in-band accuracy) costs 14-18% on GroupNorm and 44% on split var_mean vs an unrestricted selection; revisit plan choice once norms are single multi-output kernels.
2026-10-24 per-kernel breakdown (results/welford-timing.json): CubeCL kernels match or beat Triton's per kernel (split var_mean first stage 17.3-19.1 vs 18.2 us; GroupNorm f32 first stage 8.0-10.3 vs 10.4; GroupNorm pointwise 13.4 vs 14.9; LayerNorm bf16 statistics kernels 20-22 vs Triton's 39.7 stats+output kernel); short second stages 0.3-0.8 us slower (<2.5 us kernels, 6cl). The end-to-end gap is kernel count: e.g. split var_mean runs three first-stage kernels (mean, m2, weight) each repeating the reduction.
2026-10-24 (welford-reductions 7): the split Welford first stage (var_mean 8x300000, masked welford_combine over 8109-element chunks, 296 blocks) is 2-9% slower than Triton per kernel at ncu fixed clocks (19.3-20.6 vs 18.9 us; CUPTI 4-15% on the 3080, 12-14% on the 3090). Memory throughput is equal (~70%); the difference is occupancy on the tiny grid: our 256-unit blocks give 0.73 waves and 69% achieved occupancy vs Triton's 512-unit blocks at 1.45 waves and 84%. A 512-unit four-accumulator plane plan measured slower (20.4 us) and was not kept; vector loads cannot apply (chunk bases 8109*k are unaligned, as for Triton). This change replaces exactly these three single-output kernels with one, so revisit the first-stage schedule there.

Options: raise the limit (rules and descriptors are rank-generic; check launch validation and plan legality), or rely on Inductor's flattened index expressions where the kernel only needs linear addressing. This masks every later Anima gap, so rerun the Anima inventory after it.

title: Support mean/variance (Welford) reductions for GroupNorm/LayerNorm forward

title: Accept 0-d CPU scalar tensor inputs (dynamic=True lifted floats)
description: Under dynamic=True, Dynamo lifts Python float attributes into 0-d CPU float64 tensor graph inputs. The backend's input contract requires CUDA tensors and rejects the region (scoreboard: 14/18 SDXL regions, every Anima Block). Stage4 report already lists CPU scalar capture as unsupported. This masks all later gaps in those regions.
acceptance_criteria: 0-d CPU scalar inputs are passed as kernel scalar arguments (or otherwise handled) with PyTorch's type-promotion semantics preserved; SDXL/Anima regions get past the input contract in the fail-fast scoreboard; inventory rerun shows the next gaps.
notes:
Investigation 2026-10-20: the lifted floats are GroupNorm eps (Python float -> 0-d CPU float64 tensor -> .item() -> group_norm). Two layers: (1) Dynamo-level input gate (stage2/capabilities.py check_inputs: CUDA tensors only); (2) the value reaches kernels as an unbacked float symbol, which stage2 pointwise_reason rejects ('non-int64 symbolic value expression unsupported; integer shape/stride ABI only'). Needs a float-scalar kernel argument through descriptor encode, Rust replay and launcher. Inductor+Triton passes such args as fp64 (_use_fp64_for_unbacked_floats=True by default) when the device supports fp64; launcher slots are 8-byte, so a bit-cast f64 fits the existing ABI. Scratch probe relaxing only the gate: GroupNorm then fails on 'one logical reduction dimension required' (4z8.7) and the SDXL ResnetBlock on 'sum with floating accumulation only' (Welford/var_mean, new issue). Fixing this issue alone does not unblock any scoreboard region.
Implemented 2026-10-20 (uncommitted, awaiting review). Design: a 0-d CPU float64 graph input read by a GPU kernel (Inductor's unspec arg) becomes a float64 scalar declaration plus a scalar_value op; the f64 bits ride in an ordinary i64 metadata slot and the kernel reinterpret-casts them (PTX: ld.f64 + cvt.rn.f32.f64). Launch ABI, metadata builder and binding unchanged; float slots may only feed a cast and never appear in layout rules (checked in Python and Rust). The wrapper passes name.item(). GroupNorm eps never reaches a kernel: the tensorify pass raises TensorifyScalarRestartAnalysis and Dynamo specializes it; the scoreboard record-mode wrapper swallowed that signal, now fixed (status 'restarted'). Validation: 15 new tests (test_contracts_scalar_values.py), full suite 215 passed/2 skipped, equivalence 336/336, manifest PASS. Lifted bf16 arithmetic matches Inductor+Triton bit for bit but not eager (Inductor IR drops the barrier; filed 2iy). Inventory rerun (scoreboard/results/scalar-inventory, -sdxl): SDXL 18 regions = 14 Welford (12 GroupNorm, 2 GroupNorm+LayerNorm; 4z8.15), 2 multi-dim reduction (4z8.7), 2 float64 constant (4z8.8); Anima 1 = rank-5 inputs (new 4z8.16); optimizer unchanged (3 maximum/x3c, 1 mutation/4z8.9). GIL off throughout. Inventory first-step time is not comparable (regions now lower fully before rejecting).
Review 2026-10-21 (two fresh Sonnet medium reviewers: Rust/compiler/runtime; front end/scoreboard/tests). No correctness defect found. Fixed: Python checks now reject float64 into where / non-float casts and writes to 0-d CPU buffers (matching Rust); descriptor4 masked rejects float64 results; launch maps OverflowError to a scalar mismatch; from_contract defaults a missing scalar dtype to int64; test now asserts no compiles after the first value and is seeded. Left: geometry() bare-scalar grid overflow (theoretical, every grid rule has an add); reference512 producer unpack assumes sympy symbols (guarded by its length assert). After fixes: 216 passed/2 skipped, equivalence 336/336, manifest PASS.
close_reason: Lifted Python floats (0-d CPU float64 inputs) compile as float64 runtime scalar values; reviewed; 216 passed, equivalence 336/336, manifest PASS. Inventory rerun shows the next gaps (4z8.15, 4z8.7, 4z8.8, 4z8.16).

title: Adopt two tiers of rigor: cheap exploration, full qualification only for promotion
description: Every Stage 5 candidate currently runs the full gate set (required review, 18 regression groups, 168-case corpus, hash checks on 13k-17k files) even when it is a one-off diagnostic that loses. Define an exploration tier (single script, fixed clocks, ncu, shape sweep, no review, time-boxed, predeclared expected scoreboard gain and kill criterion) and keep the current qualification only for candidates that move the scoreboard.
design: Exploration tier: correctness smoke, a representative numerical check, generated-graph timing under the fixed-clock mode, and a concise retained result; predeclared expected scoreboard gain and kill criterion; time-boxed; no review. Promotion tier: full semantic corpus, invalid/rejection cases, stream/storage/lifetime controls, cache behavior, deterministic controls, machine-code evidence where relevant, full regressions, independent review.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol documented in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md and STAGE5_REPORT.md; the next exploration uses it.
notes: User decision 2026-10-20: coverage work uses exploration tier (correctness vs eager with shape sweep, numerics check, scoreboard run) until the GroupNorm milestone passes, then full qualification for promotion.

title: Make GPU timing deterministic enough to conclude
description: Clock states varying 210-1710 MHz leave most Stage 5 timing unqualified, and cwk.5 is parked as an environmental confound. Establish a measurement mode with fixed clocks: check whether nvidia-smi --lock-gpu-clocks works under WSL2, use ncu --clock-control for kernel-level comparisons, or use a native Linux host for timing runs.
acceptance_criteria: Documented measurement mode in which repeated runs of the same kernel agree within a stated spread; scoreboard and future comparisons use it.
notes:
2026-10-24 (welford-reductions 7): first-use tuning on the 3080 recorded CUPTI kernel durations 2-5x inflated in early rounds (e.g. split var_mean first stage: 0.075 ms round 1 vs 0.0196 ms round 3 for the same plan), decaying over ~100-300 ms; standalone memory-bound and matmul loops after idle showed no ramp, and tuning is single-threaded. The slow rounds made the selection gate keep plane_shared a4 (19.5 us) over plane_shared_load_batch (17.7 us) in 3 of 5 fresh-cache runs. A launch-until-stable warm-up (20-launch batches within 3%) did not fix it (stable at the slow rate) and was not kept.
2026-10-27 (4z8.28 calibration, 3080, 222 selections over three processes): 83 had a round >10% above the fastest round; compute-bound 3-20us kernels follow the SM clock between and within rounds, memory-bound 4M kernels stay within ~0.1%. Selection now pairs candidates with the baseline per round, which tolerates the drift; the clock itself is unchanged. Separate confound found: buffer placement moves a memory-bound plan by up to 2% (cubecl_torch/testing/results/selection-rule/README.md).

title: Define graceful fallback for unsupported graphs/ops without re-enabling the GIL
description: stage1/capabilities.py raises UnsupportedCubeCL with no fallback policy, so a single unsupported op makes a whole workload fail to compile. Requirement: an unsupported CubeCL lowering must not make the workload unusable, and the fallback must stay compatible with CPython 3.14t with the GIL disabled (so never Triton). The mechanism is to be established here, not presumed: options include Inductor's existing fallback/extern (ATen) paths, node-level fallback at lowering, graph partitioning, or graph-level eager fallback; prefer an existing PyTorch boundary over a new one. Note Inductor templates that require Triton (e.g. flex attention, autotuned mm templates) are a distinct gap class.
acceptance_criteria: Chosen mechanism documented with granularity and cost. Every fallback stays observable in the scoreboard: graph/kernel, CubeCL rejection reason, fallback target, count, GPU time, host time where relevant; a fallback can never silently count as CubeCL coverage. A workload containing an unsupported op runs correctly with the GIL still disabled. Rerun of 4z8.2 compares against the fail-fast baseline.
notes: Census 4z8.19 (2026-10-25): Wan 2.2 (musubi) has CPU-only regions (grid_sizes/seq_lens bookkeeping on CPU tensors) rejected with 'CUDA tensor inputs required'. Whatever fallback is chosen should cover CPU graphs (stock Inductor's CPU path or eager), not only unsupported CUDA kernels.

notes:
Preliminary from smoke runs (2026-10-20), fail-fast: (1) sdxl and anima: first region rejected 'CubeCL unsupported input contract: CUDA tensor inputs required' — under dynamic=True Dynamo lifts Python float attributes into 0-d CPU float64 tensor inputs (Stage4 report lists CPU scalar capture unsupported). (4) mode=reduce-overhead cannot be honoured: stage4 forces triton.cudagraphs=False. Inventory (record) mode on optimizer: 4/4 regions rejected (3 maximum, 1 mutation).
Full-scale fail-fast run 2026-10-20 (scoreboard/results/first-failfast, RTX 3090, clocks not fixed): all three CubeCL workloads stop at their first region (sdxl/anima: CPU float64 scalar inputs; optimizer: maximum). On both models Triton-generated kernels are ~9% of compiled-step kernel time; cuBLAS/cuDNN/flash 89-91%. Implication (single run, unfixed clocks): CubeCL kernel quality is second-order for step time; coverage and host overhead are first-order.

title: Multi-row blocks / divergence-free loops for medium rows (SDXL LayerNorm 1024x1280)
description: From wide-reduction-workgroups 6.1 (results section 6.1). SDXL float32 LayerNorm 1024x1280 (180+180 calls per step) is ~3.5% behind Triton. Triton: looped Welford, XBLOCK=2 (two rows per 512-thread block, grid 512), masked loop so every thread runs the same iterations: 4.07M instructions, 13k branches, barrier stall 17%, long scoreboard 11%. Ours (plane_shared 256x1v4): 2.85M instructions but 133k branches, barrier stall 31%, long scoreboard 30%: 1280/4 = 320 vectors over 256 units, so 64 units run a second iteration while the rest wait at the cross-plane barrier. Options: rows-per-block plans (Triton's XBLOCK), unit counts that divide the vector count, or a predicated uniform loop. Measure against Triton at 1024x1280 and 4096x1280.

title: Register-resident persistent rows (Triton's per_ kernels): short-row reductions read once, one warp per row
description: From wide-reduction-workgroups 6.1 (results section 6.1, SDXL shapes). SDXL float32 LayerNorm 4096x640 (30+30 calls per step) is ~4.6% behind Triton. Triton: triton_per_fused_native_layer_norm_0, R0_BLOCK=1024, one 32-thread warp per row, grid 4096, the row loaded once into registers, two tl.sum, no barrier: 0.61M instructions, 20,480 global load requests. Ours (plane_shared 128x1v4, welford_two_pass two sums): 4.60M instructions, 61,440 load requests (x read 3 times: sum, squared deviations, normalize), 19% barrier stall. Needs a new topology: persistent register-resident rows (plane per row, values kept across the passes), for rows Inductor reduces persistently. Likely helps every short-row reduction with a per-element pass (softmax, sum consumer, norms <= 1024).

title: Online softmax: two passes over the row as Triton, not three
description: Found in 4z8.35 / wide-reduction-workgroups. Triton's softmax kernel computes the row max and the sum of exp(x - max) in one loop (Inductor's prepare_softmax_online / online softmax: running max with rescaled sum), then writes the output in a second loop: two passes over the row. Our softmax kernel reduces max, then sum (dependent on max), then stores: three passes. At 2048x8192 float32 on the RTX 3080 (ncu, 512-unit plane_shared plan pinned) CubeCL reads 78 MB from DRAM vs Triton's 67 MB and takes 213 us vs 203 us; with 256-unit plans the third pass made it 348 us (fixed by 512-unit workgroups). Needs a combiner for the online (max, sum) pair (merge: m = max(m_a, m_b); s = s_a*exp(m_a-m) + s_b*exp(m_b-m)) and Inductor's online-softmax lowering admitted; check how CubeK and Triton/Inductor express it first (CubeK-first rule), accuracy against Triton's band (exp/rescale rounding), and timing at 300x4096 and 2048x8192.

title: LayerNorm float32 multi-output kernel 5-7% slower than Triton: second pass re-reads rows from DRAM
description: multi-output-kernels 6.1 (results/welford-timing-3080.json, -3090.json): native_layer_norm float32 4096x1280, now one kernel as Triton's, CubeCL/Triton 69.3/66.0 us (3080), 58.6/54.8 (3090); no catalog plan closes it (fastest 69.3/58.2). ncu on the 3080 at base clocks: CubeCL 70.9 us, DRAM read 23.5 MB, write 20.1 MB, L2 hit 54%, 256-thread blocks x 4096, 24 regs; Triton 65.2 us, read 21.0 MB (= the input), write 20.0 MB, L2 hit 50%, 512-thread blocks x 2048 (two rows per program), 31 regs. The gap is the per-element pass re-reading ~12% of rows from DRAM: Triton marks the first-pass loads evict_last and the second-pass loads evict_first, so rows stay in L2. bf16 LayerNorm is faster than Triton. Options: load cache-eviction hints in the emitter (check CubeCL IR support and CubeK), keep the row in registers between the reduction and the per-element pass for rows that fit, or two rows per workgroup as Triton.
notes: 2026-10-28 diagnosis (3080, ncu, plane_shared 256x1 v4, after 4z8.32): CubeCL 70.1-70.6 us, Triton 64.8. L1 global-load misses: CubeCL ~928k sectors vs Triton 683k (= x once); L2 tex reads 922-930k vs 683k; DRAM read 23.2-23.6 vs 21.1 MB. Triton (XBLOCK 2, R0_BLOCK 2048, 16 warps) re-reads x in its second loop with evict_first (first-pass x and weight/bias evict_last). Experiments patching the cached PTX of our kernel: any one hint recovers the gap - second-pass x ld.global.nc.L1::evict_first 64.4-64.5 us, ld.global.cs (= CUDA __ldcs) 65.1-65.3, first-pass evict_last only 65.1, all Triton's hints 63.9; L2 reads ~705-739k. Same with the original scalar per-element pass as with a vectorized one (vector pass alone: no gain, 70.6), so no emitter vectorization needed. CubeCL IR and CubeK have no load cache hints (only memory-pool eviction); CubeCL C++ emits plain dereferences of its own float_4 structs. Fix needs a CubeCL patch extension: a streaming/evict_first hint on LoadOp (attribute; C++ lowering via a size-dispatched __ldcs helper, other backends ignore it), set by the reduction emitter on per-element-pass loads of buffers the reduction pass already read.
close_reason: Fixed: per-element pass loads the rows the reduction pass read as streaming loads (CubeCL patch: LoadOp streaming_load attribute, CUDA ld.global.nc.L1::evict_first inline PTX; emitter marks re-reads). float32 LayerNorm 4096x1280 65.05/66.03 us (3080), 54.22/54.48 (3090); ncu 64.8-65.2 vs Triton 64.8, L2 reads 727k vs 683k. Best plan improves with the hint in all 6 pinned A/B cases. Manifest: 38 RMSNorm/training cases changed in generated code only, re-recorded. Suite 388 passed. title: Exact float fmod/remainder: large-quotient speed against Triton
description: Found in x3c group 6 (2026-10-27, RTX 3080, 4M float32, same-process controls). Our fmod/remainder use CUDA fmodf (exact, subnormals kept). With quotients up to ~1e9: our remainder 77.95 us vs our two-input control (x+y) 74.84 (+4.2%); Triton remainder 74.81 vs its control 74.39 (+0.6%), but Triton's remainder is wrong there (LLVM frem expansion: 1e10 % 3 = 256). Triton's exact fmod (libdevice, FTZ) large-q 76.1 vs ours 77.5 in the harness run (+1.8%). Small quotients: level within noise (ours +0.9% over control, Triton +0.6%). Cause not yet isolated: fmodf's reduction loop vs libdevice __nv_fmodf compiled with FTZ (Triton flushes subnormal operands: fmod(0, 2^-149) = NaN there). Candidates: an fma-based fast path for |a/b| < 2^24 plus a cheaper large-quotient reduction, compared in SASS against libdevice's FTZ fmod; keep exactness and subnormals. Acceptance: large-quotient fmod/remainder within Triton fmod's spread on both GPUs, results unchanged (test_float_remainder.py).
notes:
RTX 3090 confirmation (rounding-remainder-timing-3090.json, harness rounds): remainder large-q 65.35-66.68 vs Triton 61.71-62.40 (+7%); fmod large-q 64.91-65.58 vs 63.22-63.69 (+3%); remainder small-q 63.26-63.70 vs 61.80-62.35 (+2.3%) while our fmod small-q is level (61.87-63.16 vs 62.31-62.47), so on the 3090 the remainder sign fix-up (compares, where, add over the fmodf result) also shows ~1.2 us. Investigate both: the large-quotient reduction and whether the fix-up's selects stall behind fmodf.
2026-10-27 time-boxed look, RTX 3090, same-process interleaved controls (7 rounds, 4M float32, |a/b| up to ~100): ours x+y 61.98, fmod 63.20, remainder 63.13 us; Triton x+y 61.42, fmod 62.47, remainder 61.93. So the remainder sign fix-up costs nothing (the earlier '~1.2 us fix-up' reading was buffer placement); the small-quotient gap is ~0.56 us generic two-input (same in plain x+y) plus ~0.6 us exact fmodf over Triton's inexact frem expansion. A fast exact path (q = trunc(a/b), r = fma(-q, b, a), one correction, fmodf fallback for |a/b| >= 2^22 or specials) is exact only with a correctly rounded quotient (no undershoot by monotonic rounding; overshoot gives |r - b| <= |b|, representable) and needs copysign for a zero result of negative a; our default division is div.full, so it would need div_rn, whose cost must be measured against fmodf's.

title: Nondeterministic kernel.cu for kernels with several shared arrays (CubeCL alloc_shared_memory iterates a HashMap)
description: Found 2026-10-25 during 7lu step 2 byte checks: the same cubecl-stage0 binary run twice on one descriptor gives different kernel.cu for 25-30 of 244 matrix cases, all with more than one shared scratch array (Welford: 3 arrays, up to 3! = 6 distinct outputs). cubecl.ir is identical. Cause: .stage0-sources/cubecl crates/cubecl-opt/src/passes/alloc_shared_memory.rs:54 collects analysis.allocations.values() from a hashbrown HashMap (random per-process seed) and inserts SliceSharedOps in that order. Offsets are assigned deterministically (liveness.rs allocate_slice, declaration order), so each array keeps its offset and the kernel is semantically identical; only the declaration order and SSA names (v479/v480/v481) of the reinterpret_cast slices vary. Consequences: kernel.cu is not byte-reproducible for Welford (and any multi-scratch) kernels; the manifest corpus (Stage 5 sums, one array) cannot see it, but a Welford manifest case would flake; anything keyed on source bytes (NVRTC/PTX caching, artifact digests if they include source) misses or churns. Fix candidate: sort allocs by offset (or declaration order) before inserting slices, as a hunk in native/cubecl-fp.patch (audited patch stack; update fp_hardening/patches.py), or upstream. Repro: scratchpad matrix script from the 7lu session (descriptor matrix over strategies x sum/max/welford), comparing a binary with itself.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated runs of the compiler on every Welford plan produce byte-identical kernel.cu; a Welford case in the manifest corpus (or a dedicated determinism test) guards it; manifest PASS for existing cases.

title: Short reduction kernels slower than Triton: no persistent one-block final, sub-2us plan variance
description: Found in generic-reduction-combiners task 5.1 (RTX 3080, warm clocks, 3 alternating rounds, results in cubecl_torch/testing/results/extrema-timing.json). Max/min are level or faster than Inductor+Triton in 13/16 cases but measurably slower in 3: amax/amin fp32 2x1048579 (~3%, 15.7-16.1 vs 15.3-15.5 us) and amin bf16 37x129 (1.83-1.93 vs 1.55-1.62 us). Per-kernel breakdown: the 2x1M partial kernels are level (13.8 vs 13.7 us); the whole gap is the split's 2-output x 129-partial final kernel, which stays on shared_tree_reduction_baseline (2.09 us) vs Triton's persistent final (1.5 us); independent_planes reaches ~1.4 us on comparable 129-element rows. Cause: tuning.select replaces the frozen baseline only when best median+3MAD < baseline median-3MAD (and 2 of 3 round wins); at 1-2 us the MADs overlap, so the baseline is kept (amax bf16 37x129 happened to pick independent_planes, amin kept baseline). Not max/min-specific: sum split finals outside the reference512 pair take the same path. The rule is pinned by the inductor-backend 'Selection equivalence' requirement (Stage 5 parity under injected timings), so changing it needs a spec change. Related: sil.1 (deterministic GPU timing), sil.4.
notes:
3090 capture 2026-10-23 (display GPU, no video, warm clocks, 3 alternating rounds; cubecl_torch/testing/results/extrema-timing-3090.json): 12/16 level or faster (2x1048579 now faster: 13.0-13.3 vs 13.5-13.7 us fp32, 7.2-7.8 vs 8.8-9.1 bf16; 300x4096 4.5 vs 7.6 us). Slower beyond spread: bf16 8x65539 amax/amin ~17% (5.0-5.7 vs 4.3-4.5 us): both stages often stay on shared_tree_reduction_baseline, incl. a 256-thread tree over 9 partials vs Triton's 1.4 us persistent final (sum uses the qualified reference512/final9 pair there, max cannot) - the selection rule above. fp32 37x129 amax/amin ~0.1 us (~7%): independent_planes was selected, so this is a short-row plan-efficiency difference vs Triton's persistent reduction, not the baseline rule; on the 3080 the same case was level. 3080 capture: cubecl_torch/testing/results/extrema-timing.json. Spec reduction-kernels records these as short-kernel exceptions tracked here.

From 4z8.17 (2026-10-22): numerical bar for reduction plans is fp64 error no worse than Inductor+Triton on the same inputs (not the old eager rtol=atol=2e-5 held-out bar). Current plans already sit in Triton's band at 512..1M rows. Requalify rejected candidates (multi-accumulator = Triton's own shape, combined plane_shared, load-batch) against that bar; compensated long rows become optional. Also: Inductor split reductions are rejected ('dtype for constant unsupported: torch.int32' on x.sum(-1) for 8x65539 and 4x262147 fp32/bf16).
2026-10-22: Fixed static split rejection ('dtype for constant unsupported: torch.int32'). Cause: Inductor's ragged split mask compares index_expr(indices, int32) < index_expr(numel, int32); a static numel folds to constant(numel, int32), and index_masks.widen_mask_indices widened only the index_expr side. It now widens comparison-only int32 constants too (exact in int64). Test: test_inductor_backend::test_static_split_reduction_with_ragged_extent; the contract test's 'split_with_unsupported_index_dtype' rejection case removed. Numerics vs Inductor+Triton, x.sum(-1) fp32, 400 seeds x {randn, randn+0.5}, paired fp64 |err|: static split factors match Triton (9/33/129); static 8x65539 ratio 0.925 (z=-5.3, better), 4x262147 0.998 (z=-0.1), 2x1048579 1.041 (z=1.3, inconclusive). Dynamic 4x262147: ratio 1.054 (z=2.5) - measurably but slightly worse; cause is CubeCLChoices planning anchor picking split 32 where Triton picks 33 (pre-existing, not from this fix). Requalify the dynamic planning anchor alongside the other reduction candidates. bf16 outputs: error = output rounding on both paths.
Correction 2026-10-22, 5x larger sample (2000 seeds x 2 distributions): 2x1048579 is parity (static ratio 1.006 z=0.5, dynamic 0.990 z=-0.8). 4x262147 is measurably worse in BOTH modes: static 1.033 (z=3.6) with the same split (33) as Triton, so the gap is in the static per-partial plan for ~7944-element partials; dynamic 1.041 (z=4.3) with guarded split 32, but 1.002 (z=0.2) with split_policy=inherited (split 33), so the dynamic gap is the CubeCLChoices planning anchor. Both are floor violations to fix here. Test now uses an fp32 output so mask errors are visible and asserts the two split stages (extents 7283 and 9).
Resolution 2026-10-22 (agreed with user): forced-split comparison on dynamic 4x262147 (1000 seeds x 2 dists) shows CubeCL matches Triton at every equal split (16/31/32/33/34/64: c/t 0.98..1.03, |z|<=2.3), while the split count itself moves error up to ~10% on BOTH backends, non-monotonically (33/34 best, 31 worst). Mean error ~0.15 ulp of the output (mostly final rounding); a 4% gap is ~0.006 ulp. So the dynamic anchor (32) and the static 3% are inside Triton's own outcome band: no heuristic or plan change. Floor reading: 'measurably worse' = outside Triton's band at matched settings, not worse than its single best configuration.
2026-10-23: implemented by OpenSpec change generic-reduction-combiners (combiner abstraction in descriptor3.rs + max/min as first non-sum client). TUPLE_REDUCTION reclassified to the scan family; REDUCE_TO_SINGLE_ELEMENT n/a by default (4x9.16).

title: Audit accuracy-first backend choices against the Triton-parity goal
description: The repo spent a phase chasing accuracy beyond what Inductor+Triton does (user, 2026-10-20). The goal is now Triton parity on correctness-matched workloads (4z8.5), so choices that are stricter than Triton may be inherited from that phase rather than deliberate. Classify each as keep (with the reason it is worth its cost), relax to Triton's behaviour, or measure first. Known candidates: (1) inductor/effects.py compile_backend forces emulate_precision_casts=True (Triton default False): extra rounding ops in every low-precision kernel; also why static-float bf16 math matches eager while Triton does not. (2) Reduction numerical policy, inductor/legality.py numerical_reason: long rows must use shared_tree_compensated, and several candidates (multi-accumulator, combined plane_shared, load-batch, reference512) are rejected against a held-out accuracy bar rather than against Triton's plain fp32 accumulation. (3) Accuracy-qualification work items whose priority depends on this decision: cwk (cancellation error in reused long-row reduction), 1tc (FastMath provenance before relaxed modes). (4) The CubeCL FP patch stack (fp_hardening): check which parts go beyond Triton's actual codegen flags; do not assume, compare. Already decided: 2iy (tensorified-scalar bf16 rounding) accepts Triton parity; revisit if scoreboard error-vs-eager points at it. Use Triton's output on the same inputs as the reference when classifying.
notes:
Audit result 2026-10-22 (evidence: session scratchpad audit/evidence.md; same torch commit both venvs, fixed saved inputs, cuda:1). POINTWISE: production (emulate_precision_casts forced True + NVRTC --fmad=false + default prec-div) == eager bit-for-bit on 12 cases. emulate off + --fmad=true + --prec-div=false == Triton default bit-for-bit on all 12 (bf16/fp16 chains, explicit cast, scalar literals, exp*mul, fp32 a*b+c, exp, sqrt, recip, div, sin, cos). Eager emulation is LESS accurate vs fp64 than Triton default (double rounding: f16 chain max 6274 vs 1.15 ulp). No-FMA a*b+c on cancelling inputs up to 1.7e7 ulp vs 0.5. Division: CubeCL div.rn 0.5 ulp vs Triton div.full 2.02 ulp. exp/sqrt/sin/cos already identical. Triton default drops an explicit .to(bf16) round-trip inside a fused kernel (upstream Inductor; emulate_precision_casts is the opt-in); parity inherits that. Intent: STAGE2_REPORT 'chooses that existing eager-precision mode'; FP_HARDENING chose --fmad=false. REDUCTIONS (x.sum(-1), rows 512..1M): CubeCL current plans, Triton and eager all in the same error band vs fp64 (rel. to sum|x|); Triton long rows = RBLOCK independent lanes + tree (the multi-accumulator shape legality.py rejects). VERDICTS: relax emulate_precision_casts (stop forcing; honour Inductor config); relax --fmad (= not emulate_precision_casts, as Triton enable_fp_fusion); relax prec-div (= eager_numerics.division_rounding); keep fp_hardening simplifier removals (unsound folds, no cost) and overlay precision edits (fix Inductor's emulate mode); reduction bar -> 'fp64 error no worse than Triton on same inputs' in 4x9.6; cwk superseded; 1tc not a prerequisite (NVRTC-level, not CubeCL IR FastMath). Found: CubeCL rejects split reductions (8x65539, 4x262147: 'dtype for constant unsupported: torch.int32').
Implemented 2026-10-22 under the refined policy (Triton is a floor, keep proven improvements): emulate_precision_casts no longer forced (Inductor config honoured); fp_contract = not emulate_precision_casts captured at codegen -> NVRTC --fmad, in artifact key, tuning identity and kernel cache key; division/sqrt stay correctly rounded (stricter than Triton div.full, kept: more accurate, cost unmeasured); new overlay hunk makes graph casts to FP16/BF16 always round (Triton drops them). Production probe: bit-identical to Triton default on 10/12 cases; bf16 explicit cast == eager; div/recip correctly rounded. Equivalence harness runs package with emulate_precision_casts=True (= Stage 5 numerics): 336/336, manifest PASS. Full suite 229 passed / 2 skipped (one earlier run hit the oav timing flake, recorded there). Sonnet review: no blockers; fixes applied (host_overhead fp_contract=False, build.provenance for the key test, fp16 cast coverage, doc wording); rem/floor-under-FMA caveat recorded on x3c. Open follow-up: measure the cost of correctly rounded division vs div.full before ever relaxing it.
Correction: final full suite after review fixes = 228 passed, 2 skipped (not 229).
Cost of the remaining choices (same run as 5os): explicit graph-cast rounding kept vs dropped (Triton): cast_mem bf16 2^26 641.8 vs 640.0us (-0.3%, within noise), cast_heavy 8 bf16 round-trips 2^24 161.8 vs 157.8 (-2.5%) -> keep (respects the user's request; negligible cost). Old forced emulation vs new default: bf16_chain 812.0 vs 761.4 (new 6.6% faster), cast_heavy 198.6 vs 161.8 (new 22.7% faster), memory-bound div/recip unchanged. Division: see 5os (kept). Side observation, not numerics: with tuning=baseline (scalar plan) Triton is faster on bf16 pointwise (bf16_chain 581.9 vs 761.4us, cast_mem 588.3 vs 641.8); fp32 div/recip equal. Not yet compared under first_use tuning.
Division revised (see 5os): default div.full as Triton, eager_numerics.division_rounding opts into div.rn. Numerics(fp_contract, exact_division) replaces the fp_contract bool through tuning/kernels/build/nvrtc; nvrtc.STAGE5 = (False, True) for the equivalence harness, binding test and host_overhead. Policy wording: keep a proven improvement only when the gain is material; being measurably worse than Triton needs a material benefit.
bf16 pointwise gap check (2026-10-22, 3 alternating rounds, 2^26 elements, median CUPTI us): baseline / first_use / Triton: bf16_chain 760.7 / 582.3 / 582.5; cast_mem 642.1 / 588.2 / 589.0; bf16_add 620.5 / 580.7 / 583.1; f32_chain 1150.5 / 1150.1 / 1164.6; f32_add 1164.8 / 1164.2 / 1165.1. Under first_use tuning CubeCL equals Triton (0.99-1.00x), all near the 760 GB/s floor; the earlier 8-24% gap was the scalar baseline plan only. Nothing to file.
2026-10-28 (multi-output-kernels group 5, agreed with the user): the overlay's 'graph cast to FP16/BF16 always rounds' now applies only to casts the user wrote (FX original_aten aten._to_copy / prims.convert_element_type, or no metadata); casts a decomposition inserts (std/var result dtype) follow Triton and stay in compute precision inside fused code. Measured cause: fused bf16 (x - mean)/std rounded std to bf16 and lost to Triton on every row (~1.4x error). Also low-precision reduction results are no longer rounded before fused consumers unless emulate_precision_casts (Triton keeps them float32).
close_reason: Audit done and implemented: Inductor+Triton is a floor. Forced eager emulation removed; FMA and division follow Inductor's Triton switches (emulate_precision_casts, eager_numerics.division_rounding) via compiler.nvrtc.Numerics; graph casts to FP16/BF16 always round (deliberate deviation from Triton, cost within noise). Production matches Triton bit-for-bit on 11/12 probe cases (the 12th is the explicit cast). Suite 229 passed, equivalence 336/336, manifest PASS. Reduction bar moved to 4x9.6; cwk superseded; division cost in 5os.

notes:
2026-10-27: follows multi-output-kernels (4z8.21). Triton fuses the in-place Adam step into one kernel whose outputs alias its inputs (in_ptr/out_ptr pairs over the same storage); after the graph-level mutation work here, that kernel needs this change's several outputs plus an aliasing contract for outputs that share storage with inputs.
2026-10-28: multi-output-kernels is done: kernels can have several outputs (up to 16 buffers), so Triton's in-place optimizer kernel shape (outputs written back over input storage) needs only the graph-level mutation admission here plus an aliasing contract for outputs over input storage (the runtime currently refuses an output sharing storage with an input). In-kernel storage reuse is separate: 4z8.31.

Decide whether to accept Triton parity here or add backend-side barriers; test: cubecl_torch/testing/test_contracts_scalar_values.py (bf16 case asserts the single-rounding result).
close_reason: Decided 2026-10-20: accept Inductor+Triton parity. The deviation from eager comes from Inductor's tensorify_python_scalars pass (a Python scalar becomes a 0-d tensor op, so the scalar is converted to bf16 and no barrier follows), which runs before any backend; CubeCL output is bit-identical to Triton's. A backend fix would have to guess intent the IR no longer carries and would change kernels where Inductor already places barriers. Note the backend otherwise exceeds Triton via forced emulate_precision_casts, so this accepts the weaker guarantee here. Revisit if scoreboard error-vs-eager points at it; fixes would be upstream or specialize_float=True per workload. Tracked in the accuracy-vs-parity audit.

title: cubecl_torch test/harness hygiene from consolidation review
description:
From the 2026-10-20 sil.5 review:
- Contract tests use start=len(trace.EVENTS) then list(EVENTS)[start:] on a bounded deque (LIMIT 10000): rotation makes the offset wrong; iterating while another thread appends can raise on free-threaded Python. Add a sequence counter or scoped capture to runtime/trace.py.
- equivalence.py compares outputs only under baseline; first_use plans are compared by IR/CUDA/PTX digest only. Comparing first_use outputs needs the baseline-detected nondeterministic keys.
- Injected timings are constant per candidate, so the 2-of-3 vote / MAD margin of real selection is exercised only by test_contracts_tuning.py (recorded in design.md).
- gate_assertions.py extraction is AST call-name exact: reject( (stage5/launch_controls.py, 10 calls) and non-Assertion raises are not inventoried; the reviewer checked those are covered.
- Scoreboard parity (task 8.1) was checked manually; dynamo.inductor_counters differs between first-* and package-* results and was not investigated.
- test_fp_rewrites_rust_suite (13 live sites) runs only with CUBECL_TORCH_SLOW=1.

title: cubecl_torch runtime/compiler hardening from consolidation review
description:
Low-severity items from the 2026-10-20 sil.5 review, all matching Stage 5 behaviour (not regressions):
- runtime/launch.py batch() replays _prepared args without re-validation or launch_check (offline timing only).
- runtime/launch.py _metadata dict is unbounded (one device tensor per distinct spans/info key); dynamic-shape workloads leak small allocations. _layouts is LRU 64.
- runtime/launch.py _validate coerces float/bool scalars with int() (64.9 launches as 64); consider operator.index.
- LoadedKernel(device=torch.device('cuda')) without index refuses every launch (fails closed).
- runtime/artifact.py from_contract does not validate rule trees (negative scalar slot indexes from the end).
- compiler/build.py identity() is @cache'd: rebuilding native libs in a long-lived process keeps the stale identity; identity includes GPU UUID and absolute NVRTC path (over-keying).
- compiler: descriptor schema family (3 reduction / 4 pointwise) vs plan family not cross-checked at compile time; Stage 5 only checked in legality.structural_reason for vector/final plans. Check what the Rust compiler does with a mismatch first.
- inductor/overlay.py: an already published tree is trusted on overlay.json equality; not re-verified against file hashes.

title: Deterministic embedding/scatter backward without float atomics
description: Embedding backward (and scatter_add with colliding indices) uses float atomic_add, so gradients are not bitwise reproducible run to run (Stage 5 and cubecl_torch alike; 3 runs -> 3 digests in the equivalence harness). Deterministic mode already reselects the ATen extern path. Consider a sort + segmented-reduction kernel for the default path if reproducible training runs need it. Behaviour/perf change; out of scope for the consolidation.

title: Compilation during training: serialized compiler service with safe publication
description: Trainer answers: compilation may happen mid-run (new shapes, newly used capabilities, encoder producers), and unrelated execution should continue. Do not assume arbitrary simultaneous torch.compile calls are safe: serialize or isolate the compiler service, and publish new executable state only after verification without replacing state still in use. Test CubeCL compilation (Rust/NVRTC/cache) while other threads launch kernels on the GIL-free runtime.
acceptance_criteria: A concurrency test compiles new CubeCL regions while other threads run existing kernels; no crashes, wrong results or GIL re-enable.

title: Quantized base + adapter workload from an intended implementation
description: Trainer answers: FP8/INT8/other quantized bases are intended coverage, each with a concrete implementation/profile; storage, compute precision and trainability are separate choices. A frozen or quantized base still passes gradients to adapters. Start with one actual intended quantized-base-plus-adapter integration; native low-precision training and QAT are separate later items.
acceptance_criteria: One quantized-base + LoRA workload runs with gradients through the frozen base, on all three paths.

title: Consolidate Stage5 findings into the existing main report
description: Make STAGE5_REPORT.md the single current starting point and mark follow-up reports as historical/supporting evidence. Preserve original report bodies and artifact paths; connect project-memory findings to this entry point. Documentation only, no new experiment, report proliferation or numerical-policy change.
close_reason: Consolidated current findings in STAGE5_REPORT.md; eight supporting records link back. Original bodies preserved verbatim, report links and diff whitespace verified, and bd prime injects canonical entry-point guidance.

title: Bound immutable CUDA metadata retention without weakening stream readiness
description: The Stage5 launch follow-up bounds only descriptor layouts at 64 scalar keys. The Stage0/2 _metadata_cache and _metadata_complete intentionally retain CUDA tensors/events for every prepared scalar/length key for process lifetime. Review confirmed this is pre-existing, not a new regression. Investigate a bounded policy separately, preserving InfoBuilder identity, CUDA event generation/readiness, current-stream waits, record_stream and prepared-batch ownership. Eviction must invalidate completion for the evicted metadata generation. No change included in the bounded warm-dispatch experiment. See STAGE5_LAUNCH_REPORT.md and stage5/artifacts/launch/review-disposition.md.
notes: 2026-10-20 (4z8.6): float64 runtime scalar values (lifted Python floats) now ride in metadata slots, so every distinct value is a new metadata key: one H2D upload plus a retained CUDA tensor per value. Constant values (GroupNorm eps) are fine; a per-step changing float (e.g. a lifted learning rate in a compiled optimizer step) would grow the cache every step. Raises the priority of bounding this once such workloads compile.

title: Keep Stage4 effectful fusion and device-failure diagnostics as explicit follow-up boundaries
description: Stage4 bounded gate passes; follow-up only, not a missing acceptance requirement. RNG/indirect fusion stays vetoed pending effect-safe replay proof; arbitrary user-visible mutations, capture and concurrent compilation remain unsupported; invalid indirect indices trap with asynchronous CUDA719 rather than eager assertion diagnostics. Preserve STAGE4_REPORT.md contracts and existing compiler/launcher/FP policy. Do not silently broaden these boundaries during performance work.

title: Report upstream: addcdiv(value=1) misses Inductor's FMA/div_rn lowering
description: Measured 2026-10-26 (pinned torch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0). torch.addcdiv is CompositeImplicitAutograd, so Dynamo hands Inductor add(s, mul(div(a, b), v)); post_grad.py _fuse_addcdiv_to_fma rebuilds aten.addcdiv so lowering.py addcdiv emits div_rn (+ fma for v != 1) to match eager CUDA. With value=1 the joint-graph remove_no_ops (joint_graph.py) has already deleted the '* 1', the pattern no longer matches, and the kernel is s + a / b with Triton's approximate division: ~1 ulp from eager in 355/1024 float32 rows (cubecl_torch/testing/data/float_arithmetic_triton.pt, case addcdiv-value1-float32). Looks unintended (the lowering's own docstring handles value=1). Report to pytorch/pytorch with a minimal repro; a fix would add an add(s, div(a, b)) pattern or run the re-fusion before remove_no_ops. Our backend inherits the behaviour (spec float-arithmetic, scenario 'addcdiv with value 1').
notes: 2026-10-26: cubecl_torch is not affected: its backend sets joint_graph_constant_folding=False (Stage 2, because remove_no_ops also rewrites x + 0 and loses -0.0), so the '* 1' survives, _fuse_addcdiv_to_fma fires and value=1 divides with div_rn, bitwise eager. The upstream report still applies to default Inductor+Triton.

title: Drop stage names from native messages at the next compiler rebuild
description: Left from oce (2026-10-26): native/src/plan.rs 'unsupported Stage5 semantic schema' and native/launcher.c 'unsupported Stage5 launch geometry'. Changing them rebuilds the compiler binary (new digest, every cached artifact rebuilds), so fold them into the next deliberate native change or CubeCL upgrade rather than rebuilding for text alone.

title: Watch: NVIDIA cuda-oxide / cutile-rs / CUDA Tile IR (reference only)
description:
Reference note so we know these exist. Decision (2026-10-25): CubeCL/CubeK stays the backend; neither project is a dependency candidate.

- cuda-oxide (https://github.com/NVlabs/cuda-oxide, book https://nvidia.github.io/cuda-rust/cuda-oxide/): NVIDIA's experimental rustc codegen backend, Rust -> PTX, SIMT model, single-source host/device. v0.1 alpha (May 2026). Ahead-of-time rustc compile per kernel, so it doesn't fit our runtime descriptor -> CubeCL IR -> NVRTC path.
- cutile-rs (https://github.com/NVlabs/cutile-rs, paper https://research.nvidia.com/publication/2026-06_fearless-concurrency-gpu): research demo of the CUDA Tile model in Rust. A proc macro captures the kernel AST, which is JIT-compiled via CUDA Tile IR to a cubin. Reports ~96% of cuBLAS GEMM on B200.

Revisit triggers, as references only, not adoption:
1. PyTorch cuTile RFC (https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/175311) lands a TileKernel hierarchy in Inductor, which would affect our SIMDKernel adapter.
2. CUDA Tile IR supports sm_86 (Ampere), making it a useful accuracy/speed comparison for matmul/attention tiles alongside Triton and CubeK.

Close if neither has happened by the defer date and nothing else makes it relevant.

title: Run the accuracy and timing harness on rented cloud GPUs
description:
Deferred until the backend is mature on the local RTX 3080/3090 (sm_86): other GPUs add nothing before then.

Approach: a container image built from the repo (both venvs: free-threaded 3.14t with pinned PyTorch for CubeCL, and the Triton reference env; the native compiler binary; the audited .stage0-sources/cubecl checkout with native/cubecl-fp.patch, which the build checks). Kernels are generated by NVRTC at run time, so nothing can be prebuilt for another device. One entry script regenerates the Triton reference on the target GPU (Triton's block sizes and splits are per device), runs the band sweep and timing (optionally suite and equivalence), and packs the JSON results for download; a local script compares devices. Cloud hosts with root on native Linux can lock clocks (nvidia-smi -lgc), which also helps sil.1.

First step: audit for sm_86 assumptions (warp size 32 / plane width, shared-memory and launch limits in launcher.c, capability checks) before renting anything other than Ampere.
acceptance_criteria: An image and entry script that produce the band/timing JSON on a non-sm_86 GPU without local edits; the architecture audit's findings recorded.
